items.memo:
BILL NUMBER: S6116

SPONSOR: SAVINO
 
TITLE OF BILL:  An act to amend the election law, in relation to
authorizing a change of party affiliation 25 days prior to the next
ensuing primary, general or special election, overhauling campaign
financing and providing a voluntary financing program for campaigns for
state officers; to amend the general business law, in relation to
authorizing the imposition of an additional surcharge on recoveries for
fraudulent practices relating to stocks, bonds and other securities; to
amend the state finance law, in relation to establishing the New York
state campaign finance fund and providing for transfers thereto from the
abandoned property fund; to amend the tax law, in relation to providing
for a New York state campaign finance fund check-off; and to repeal
certain provisions of the election law relating thereto

 
PURPOSE:

This bill would provide candidates for the nomination for election or
election to all statewide and legislative offices, as well as delegates
to a constitutional convention, the option of receiving matching funds
in return for agreeing to: (i) limits on contributions; (ii) strict
eligibility requirements; (iii) participation in debates; and (iv) the
monitoring and auditing of campaign expenditure s by an independent
campaign finance board within the board of elections.

In addition, this bill requires the reporting to the campaign finance
board of all independent expenditures; caps individual campaign contrib-
utions to $2,600; bans campaign contributions from corporations; creates
a New York State Business Contract Database; and bans transfers between
political party committees and candidate committees.

 
SUMMARY OF PROVISIONS:

Section 1 provides a short title, the "Integrity in Elections Act of
2016". Section 2 provides for the legislative intent.

Section 3 amends Subdivision 5-304 of election law allowing for change
of enrollment within 25 days of an election

Section 4 amends section 14-100 of the Election Law to refer to "board,"
"state board" or "state board of elections" as the "campaign finance
board."

Section 5 amends section 14-102 of the Election Law to define an electi-
oneering communication and to increase reporting requirements related to
independent expenditures.

Section 6 amends section 14-114 of the Election Law to provide that any
contribution to any state or local candidate in both a primary and a
general election would be capped at $2,600.

Section 7 repeals subdivision 6 of section 14-114 of the Election law
related to contribution limits.

Section 8 amends section 14-114 of the Election Law to reduce the
contribution to a party or constituted committee from $62,500 to
$10,000.

Section 9 amends subdivision two of section 14-116 of the Election Law
to prohibit a candidate or political committee from accepting a loan
unless expressly permitted, and prohibits corporations, including limit-
ed liability companies, from making political contributions to candi-
dates.

Section 10 repeals subdivision three of section 14-124 of the Election
Law in order to apply contribution and receipt limits to party house-
keeping accounts.

Section 11 adds a new section 14-125 to the Election Law to establish
the New York State Business Contract Database.

Section 12 renames Article 14 of the Election Law as "Campaign Finance".

Section 13 designates a new "Title 1" within Article 14 of the Election
Law and its new title heading "Campaign Receipts and Expenditures".

Section 14 establishes a new "Title 2" within Article 14 of the Election
Law, adding new sections 14-200 through 14-228, collectively known as
the "Matching Financing" program:

Section 14-200 defines those terms applicable to Title 2 and limits
their application to candidates for the nomination for election or for
the election to the offices of Governor, Lieutenant Governor, State
Comptroller, Attorney General, member of the Assembly, State Senate and
delegate to a constitutional convention;

Section 14-202 requires every participating candidate to have only one
authorized committee to receive matching funds and to notify the state
board of elections of such authorized committee and any other reports as
the State Board of Election currently requires;

Section 14-204 limits the amount a candidate can receive from any one
contributor for both a primary and a general election to $2,600 per
election cycle;

Section 14-206 requires all participating candidates to maintain records
of receipts and expenditures for any general election;

Section 14-208 lists the requirements necessary to be eligible for the
optional campaign finance program including:

The receipt of at least $650,000 in matchable contributions from at
least 6,500 contributors in amounts of no more than $250 for the Office
of Governor in a primary or general election;

The receipt of at least $200,000 in matchable contributions from at
least 2,000 contributors in amounts of no more than $250 for the Office
of Lieutenant Governor in a primary and for the Offices of State Comp-
troller and Attorney General in a primary or a general election;

The receipt of at least $20,000 in matchable contributions of no more
than $250 for the State Senate in a primary, special or general election
including at least $10,000 from at least 100 contributors residing in
the Senate district for which the seat is to be filled;


The receipt of at least $10,000 in matchable contributions of no more
than $250 for the State Assembly in a primary, special or general
election including at least $5,000 from at least 50 contributors who
reside in the Assembly district for which the seat is to be filled;

The receipt of not less than $20,000 in matchable contributions of no
more than $250 for the election of an at-large delegate to a constitu-
tional convention; and

The receipt of not less than $5000 in matchable contributions of no more
than $250 from at least 50 contributors residing in the district for
which a district delegate to a constitutional convention is to be
elected.

Section 14-212 authorizes the payment of matching funds to an eligible
participating candidate in an amount of six dollars for every dollar in
a matchable contribution raised by a participating candidate. Matching
funds are only available for the first $250 contributed by each donor
who is a natural person residing in the State.  Total matching funds are
limited to:

An amount of $5.5 million for a primary and $8.25 million for a general
election for the Office of Governor;

An amount of $2.75 million. for a primary for the Office of Lieutenant
Governor, State Comptroller and State Attorney General and $4.125
million for the State Comptroller and Attorney General in a general
election;

An amount of $825,000 for the State Senate for a primary and for a
general election; An amount of $412,500 for the Assembly for a primary
and for a general election;

An amount of $175,000 for an at-large delegate to a constitutional
convention in a primary and in a general election; and An amount of
$50,000 for a district delegate to a constitutional convention in a
primary and in a general election.

Section 14-214 defines the uses for which matching funds may be
expended;

Section 14-216 establishes a seven-member campaign finance board within
the State Board of Elections. The chair of the Board shall be appointed
by the Governor with the advice and consent of the State Senate. Other
members shall be appointed by the Temporary President of the Senate, the
Speaker of the Assembly, the Minority Leader of the Senate, the Minority
Leader of the Assembly, attorney general, and state comptroller. Each
member shall serve for a term of six years after the initial staggered
appointments have expired;

Section 14-218 authorized the Campaign Finance Board to audit all
matters related to the Matching Financing Program;

Section 14-220 sets forth the wrongful acts that could result in the
Campaign Finance Board imposing civil fines in the amount of $5,000 or
$10,000.


Section 14-222 sets forth the criminal penalties, misdemeanors and a
class E felony that if proven, could lead to fines and imprisonment;

Section 14-224 requires the Campaign Finance Board to submit a report
every two years, beginning February 1, 2019, to the Governor and to the
legislative leaders. The report must analyze the implementation of the
matching financing program and provide recommendations for any modifica-
tion to the program;

Section 14-226 requires participating candidates to participate in at
least one debate before a primary and one debate before a general
election unless the candidate is unopposed; and

Section 14-228 provides guidelines for the distribution of funds from
the Campaign Finance Fund created pursuant to this Chapter.

Section 15 adds a new section 16-103 to election law provides that any
question or issue relating to eligibility or the payment of matching
funds may be contested in a proceeding instituted in the State Supreme
Court in Albany County.

Section 16 adds a new section 359-gg to the General Business Law to
assess, in addition to any penalty authorized by section 359-g of the
General Business Law or any damages or other compensation recoverable,
an additional surcharge in the amount of ten percent of the total penal-
ty, damages or settlement. Such surcharge would be deposited into the
Campaign Finance Fund.

Section 17 amends the State Finance Law to create a new section 99-hh
establishing the New York State Campaign Finance Fund, which would be in
the joint custody of the state comptroller and commissioner of taxation
and finance.

Section 18 adds a new section 630-g to the Tax Law to create a campaign
finance fund tax check-off on personal income tax returns, the proceeds
of which would also be deposited into the Campaign Finance Fund.

Section 19 amends section 95 of the State Finance Law to authorize the
transfer of monies from the Abandoned Property Fund to the Campaign
Finance Fund upon voucher or warrant of the Chairman of the Campaign
Finance Board.

Section 20 Repeals Section 6-120 of the election law Section 21 provides
for severability.

Section 22 provides that this Act shall take effect December 31, 2019
provided that all candidates for election in this Act will be eligible
to participate in the optional campaign finance system beginning with
the 202-general election.

 
JUSTIFICATION:

This bill provides for a voluntary campaign finance program by which
small contributions are matched on a six to one basis. This voluntary
program would expand the pool of potential candidates for office by
allowing those with limited means to be able to finance a campaign,
either for Governor, Lieutenant Governor, State Comptroller, Attorney

General, State Senator, a member of the Assembly, or a delegate to a
constitutional convention.

This bill would also cap campaign contributions to $2,600 for all state
and local candidates thereby removing the influence that large campaign
donors may have in a candidate's campaign or on an elected official. In
addition this act bans unlimited transfers from party committees to
candidate committees, by treating the party as just another contributor,
subject to the $2,600 contribution limit.

 
LEGISLATIVE HISTORY:

Similar to:

2013: 54897 (Klein) - referred to Elections Committee
2014: S4897 (Klein) - referred to Elections Committee
2016:57056 (Klein) - referred to Elections Committee

 
FISCAL IMPACT:

To be determined

 
EFFECTIVE DATE:
This Act shall take effect December 31, 2019 , provided that all candi-
dates for election in this Act will be eligible to participate in the
optional campaign finance system beginning with the 2020 general
election.

summary: Enacts the "integrity in elections act of 2019"; authorizes a change of party affiliation not less than 25 days prior to the next ensuing primary, general or special election; requires the majority vote of the entire party committee for the jurisdiction in which a candidate for public office is running, in order to nominate such candidate as the party candidate; prohibits the transfer of funds between a candidate and committees not formed for the purposes of such candidate; limits independent expenditures for political purposes; limits contributions to $2,600 to any single candidate during an election cycle; enacts campaign finance reform to provide for matching funds for the campaigns of state elected officials; authorizes the imposition of an additional surcharge on recoveries for fraudulent practices regarding stocks, bonds and other securities; establishes the New York state campaign finance fund; provides for a New York state campaign finance fund check-off.
